headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared data-engineering workflows can leak or corrupt artifacts, but both agents are docs-only and no direct interaction evidence is provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can pass artifacts and parameters into downstream steps, while dbt-core consumes warehouse inputs and model files. No shared channel is documented here, so prompt-injection-style hijack is not proven; however, if operators bridge them via shared files or copied outputs, one agent’s content could influence the other.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge, then injected instructions can propagate.
IF either agent treats upstream text artifacts as trusted instructions, then malicious content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Strip instructions from artifacts before handoff.
Use a fixed schema for inter-agent payloads.
Review any copied text before pasting.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, and dbt-core touches data warehouse data. If they share a workspace or warehouse-connected files, sensitive warehouse content can flow into workflow artifacts or logs. The profiles do not show direct leakage by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same shared workspace, then warehouse data can be copied into workflow artifacts.
IF dbt-core outputs warehouse-derived files that Argo Workflows stores or logs, then those contents may be retained outside the warehouse.
mitigations: Limit shared paths to non-sensitive files.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks on handoff files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows exposes REST and gRPC APIs and dbt-core calls a data warehouse API, so overlapping mutable operations are possible only if an operator points both at the same resources. The profiles do not show shared write scopes or locking, so conflict risk exists but is limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared warehouse objects or files, then concurrent updates can conflict.
IF an orchestrator runs both without locking, then one agent can overwrite the other’s outputs.
mitigations: Add lock files or warehouse transactions.
Check for stale outputs before overwrite.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo Workflows can produce artifacts that dbt-core may consume as inputs, creating a plausible chain where one agent’s output becomes the other’s input. Because no verification step is documented and both profiles are docs-only, the interaction is inferred rather than observed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF dbt-core consumes artifacts generated by Argo Workflows without validation, then upstream mistakes can cascade.
IF Argo Workflows schedules dbt runs based on prior outputs, then a bad artifact can trigger repeated downstream errors.
mitigations: Validate handoff files against a schema.
Compare outputs against expected row counts.

E_compliance.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, while dbt-core touches data warehouse data. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is only a low-probability gap if operators route regulated data through both systems without aligned policies.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents, then mismatched retention or residency policies can apply.
IF warehouse exports are stored as workflow artifacts, then artifact retention may exceed warehouse policy.
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in artifacts.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement at handoff points.
